resume: Tape keyboard in the style of the Mellotron M400: each key has its own tape that runs while you press and that a spring returns on release. It plays real Mellotron tapes (flute, choir, cello, vibraphone) and a piano, with old-tape lo-fi effects. Two sounds can be blended.

commandes.role: Effects page: vibrato, echo, reverb (the last knob is always MIX). Held 0.6 s, switches the effects in or out of the circuit.
LAYER page: a second sound on the other track of the tape (SOUND, MIX, OCTAVE, DETUNE). On this page, SEL changes the sound. In step recording, SEL is a rest.
HOLD: notes stay after release until the next chord. Held 0.6 s, half speed: tapes one octave lower and twice as long.
LOFI page (TAPE and WEAR: tape wear). Held 0.6 s, switches lo-fi in or out of the circuit.
Speaker equalizer page. Held 0.6 s, sets it flat (FLAT), and again to restore it.
SETUP page: tempo, fine tuning, note length, screen appearance. A second press opens SOUNDS.
PLAY page (TONE, PITCH, ATTACK, RELEASE). A new press goes to the next sound.
Saves (the device also saves by itself).
Arpeggiator page (MODE, RATE, OCTAVES, GATE). Turns the arpeggiator on or off.
16-step sequencer of at most four notes per step (LENGTH, GATE, STEP, SWING).
Records into the sequencer. When stopped, step recording.
The hand on the tape reel.
Chooses the sound: A FLUTE, B CHOIR, C CELLO, D VIBES, E PIANO.
Sets the tempo, from any page.

gestes: LFO, FX, EDIT or ENV held 0.6 s: the button's alternate action.
SEL held 1 s in step recording: clears the pattern.
a_savoir: The Mellotron tapes are those by Bernie Kornowicz (Taijiguy), free to use but not for commercial software.
The piano is not a Mellotron tape.
